chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: There are different types of loops in JavaScript.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: The most common is a for loop.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: For loops run for a specific amount of times.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: We begin with the word for, then within parentheses we have three items separated by semicolons.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: The first is the initial expression, then the condition, then the increment expression.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: After that we have the code being executed within curly braces.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: The initialization is only run once to set up the loop variable, then every time the

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: loop iterates the condition is evaluated to determine whether the code should be executed

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: or not.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: Lastly, the final expression is evaluated at the end of each loop iteration and is usually

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: used to increment or decrement the loop counter.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: Here is an example.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: We have a blank array called numbers, then in the for loop we are creating the variable

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: i and setting it to 0.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: This will be our loop counter.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: After the semicolon we check to see if i is less than 5.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: If the statement is true the loop will continue, if it is false the loop will end.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: Then after the next semicolon we are incrementing i by 1.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: Plus plus just means add 1.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: Now in our expression code we are pushing i into our numbers array.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: After the code executes the final expression runs incrementing i.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: So now i is 1 and we check our condition.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: Since i is still less than 5 we run our code again, incrementing i again and so on.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: So i will go from 0 to 1, 2, 3, 4 and then it gets to 5.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: Since i is now equal to 5 the loop stops and in our console log we get the array of 0,

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: For loops have a break early feature.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: So if for some reason you want the loop to end early you can use the break keyword.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: So here we are doing a secondary check within our code to see if i is greater than 2 and

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: if so we are ending the loop early.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: In the console log here we only get the array of 0, 1 and 2.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: A common use case for loops is looping through an array to get the values.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: So here we have an array of numbers and we are looping through it.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: The for loop is setup very similar except for the condition.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: Here we are checking to see if i is less than the array.length.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: So once we have looked at each value in the array we want the loop to stop.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: In the console log we are getting each value.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: One last example is looping through a multi-dimensional array.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: To do this we can use nested loops.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: The first loop is looping through the first dimension of the array which includes 3 levels.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: The second loop is looping through each of these arrays.

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: So then we console log the array with two indices and we end up with the numbers in

chunks.title: JavaScript For Loops
chunks.text: order 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6.

text: There are different types of loops in JavaScript. The most common is a for loop. For loops run for a specific amount of times. We begin with the word for, then within parentheses we have three items separated by semicolons. The first is the initial expression, then the condition, then the increment expression. After that we have the code being executed within curly braces. The initialization is only run once to set up the loop variable, then every time the loop iterates the condition is evaluated to determine whether the code should be executed or not. Lastly, the final expression is evaluated at the end of each loop iteration and is usually used to increment or decrement the loop counter. Here is an example. We have a blank array called numbers, then in the for loop we are creating the variable i and setting it to 0. This will be our loop counter. After the semicolon we check to see if i is less than If the statement is true the loop will continue, if it is false the loop will end. Then after the next semicolon we are incrementing i by 1. Plus plus just means add 1. Now in our expression code we are pushing i into our numbers array. After the code executes the final expression runs incrementing i. So now i is 1 and we check our condition. Since i is still less than 5 we run our code again, incrementing i again and so on. So i will go from 0 to 1, 2, 3, 4 and then it gets to Since i is now equal to 5 the loop stops and in our console log we get the array of 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. For loops have a break early feature. So if for some reason you want the loop to end early you can use the break keyword. So here we are doing a secondary check within our code to see if i is greater than 2 and if so we are ending the loop early. In the console log here we only get the array of 0, 1 and 2. A common use case for loops is looping through an array to get the values. So here we have an array of numbers and we are looping through it. The for loop is setup very similar except for the condition. Here we are checking to see if i is less than the array.length. So once we have looked at each value in the array we want the loop to stop. In the console log we are getting each value. One last example is looping through a multi-dimensional array. To do this we can use nested loops. The first loop is looping through the first dimension of the array which includes 3 levels. The second loop is looping through each of these arrays. So then we console log the array with two indices and we end up with the numbers in order 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6. This has been a 90ish second JavaScript January.
